business: ACHV Performance Systems (Hevadex Malta): 'Protected Handover', peelable OMNIGUARD protection of installed glazing and aluminium/PVC joinery, applied by ACHV-approved applicators with a signed QA handover pack
by_role: Technical director of a glazing contractor
by_process: Trial on one floor or one block first
by_current_option: Relies on the factory film already on the aluminium profiles
Self-adhesive film, plastic sheet or board with tape, applied and removed by own labour
No protection; cleans, polishes or replaces damaged items at snagging
Another peelable or spray-on protective coating
why_not: We use the factory film on the frames at no extra cost and it covers most of the programme. About €19/m² for a coating on the glass is a big jump from nothing, and I can't see where it pays back in fewer callbacks.

I pay about 12 a square metre today with film and my own lads, and this is 19 plus a minimum job size and a deposit. The aluminium already comes with factory film, so I'd be paying 60% more to fix a problem I mostly manage with snagging.

The aluminium already comes with factory film, and what protection we add is decided by the main contractor in the subcontract package, not by me. At about 19 a m2 against 12 today, I would be paying more to change something that works and that I have used for years.

The glazing subcontractor is responsible for damage until handover, not me, so I have no budget line for this. On small jobs I just tape or film the frames myself if I want to, and I buy the cheapest thing that works.

The aluminium arrives with factory film and my lads put sheet and tape on for about €12 a m². You want €19 a m² for something I already handle, plus a 50% deposit up front. I don't see where that pays me back.

I spend about 1,800 a year on snagging damage, and you want 19 euro a m2 which is 19,000 on a 1,000 m2 year. That is ten times my loss, and the main contractor is not paying me extra to protect glazing.

I pay about 12 a square metre today with my own lads and it works. This is around 19, so more than half again, and I still carry the risk if it marks a frame. I'm not changing something that works for that.

We don't buy this today and I'm not creating a new budget line and a new supplier for a coating I'd have to trust on our clients' frames. If it marks the frame or the glass when it comes off, I'm left carrying it, and at about €19 per m² it costs more than the damage it prevents on our small jobs.

ACHV is a contractor too, and I don't want a competitor on my site seeing my programme and my clients. We don't buy this today, so it would also mean a new supplier and a new budget line for a job we already handle with cheap film and tape.

I've never seen this used in Malta and I don't pay for window protection today. €19 per m² is real money on a small house job and I'd have to absorb it or argue it with the client. We tape and board the frames ourselves.

Protection of glazing is specified in the subcontract package, so the developer or main contractor decides what is done and who pays. I have no budget line for this, and a 50% deposit on a supplier I don't know is not how I operate.

We pay suppliers at 60 to 90 days, not 50% up front, and a credit check on top is a non-starter. We spend about 9k a year on snagging damage from contingency, and 19 per m2 across a block would cost more than the damage it prevents.

Protection of glazing is set in the subcontract package by the developer or main contractor, not by me. I am a site manager and cannot start a new budget line and a new supplier on my own. Film and tape cost us next to nothing.
